messages:
Taylor B: hey team :wave: on day 2 — i'm remote and on an iPhone personal hotspot. i can SSH to bastion but my dev tool can't reach internal feature-store API (10.12.8.30:9000) from my laptop. host curl to 10.12.8.30 via ssh tunnel works, but app => api fails with TLS handshake errors. any ideas?
Mina K: welcome! quick check: from the host can you `curl -v https://10.12.8.30:9000/health` and also show `ifconfig`/`ipconfig`? might be MTU or NAT hairpin problem with the hotspot.
Taylor B: host curl via tunnel works:
```
$ curl -v https://localhost:9000/health
* Connected to localhost (127.0.0.1) port 9000 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
but the app (running as a local binary) tries `https://10.12.8.30:9000` and fails with `tls: oversized record received with length 20527`.
Sam M: `oversized record` usually means MTU/fragmentation or a proxy returning plain text. Since you said SSH tunnel works, app's direct path is hitting the hotspot NAT which may not support hairpin NAT to the VPN. Two options: 1) run local port forward to bastion and point app at `localhost:9000` (quick), 2) lower MTU to avoid fragmentation: `sudo ifconfig en0 mtu 1300` (mac) or `sudo ip link set dev wlp3s0 mtu 1300` (linux) and retry, 3) set app to use the SSH SOCKS proxy: `ssh -D 1080 taylor@bastion.redwood.com` and set `ALL_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080`.
IT Ops: also note some carriers block hairpin/NAT loopback; your app's IP path may be going out through the carrier then getting blocked or translated. The SSH SOCKS proxy or explicit local `-L` forward is the safest. If using WireGuard or our corp VPN client on the host, try lowering the WireGuard MTU on the client side (eg `MTU = 1200`) — fragmented TLS can produce that error.
Taylor B: tried `sudo ifconfig en0 mtu 1300` — app still fails. started `ssh -D 1080 bastion` and set `ALL_PROXY` to `socks5://localhost:1080` and the app's requests now succeed.
Mina K: great. we'll add a short note to onboarding: "If on mobile hotspot and seeing TLS/fragmentation errors or timeouts, try SSH SOCKS proxy or lower MTU; mobile carriers often block hairpin NAT"
infra-bot: ticket INF-5200 created to add "hotspot + MTU + hairpin NAT" troubleshooting to onboarding docs (assigned eng-infra).
Taylor B: thanks folks! SOCKS proxy is a good enough workaround while i'm on the road :tada:
